steps.say: A stricture months after gallbladder surgery usually announces itself with yellowing and fevers. The bile duct was nicked or clipped during the cholecystectomy and has now scarred shut. MRCP maps the exact level without any invasive test. Short narrowings are stretched and stented from below, while long or high ones need a surgical join to bowel.
steps.tx: **Postoperative stricture** (scarred bile duct healing after cholecystectomy) declares itself months later with cholestasis and cholangitis, and MRCP maps the level before any intervention. Short lesions yield to endoscopic dilation with **multiple stenting** (several parallel plastic stents left for a year), while long or hilar narrowings need hepaticojejunostomy.

steps.say: Primary sclerosing cholangitis scars the whole biliary tree into beads, and seven in ten sufferers also have ulcerative colitis. The liver marches toward cirrhosis while the ducts keep narrowing. One in ten of these patients grows bile duct cancer, so scopes and scans never stop. Transplant is the only exit once the liver fails.
steps.tx: **Primary sclerosing cholangitis** (fibrosing bile duct disease) shows **beaded ducts** (alternating strictures and dilatations) with **ulcerative colitis** (bowel inflammation) in **70** percent, marching toward cirrhosis while **10 to 15** percent develop cholangiocarcinoma. Bowel and bile duct surveillance run together lifelong.

steps.say: Within PSC, one segment can tighten far worse than the rest, and that dominant stricture must be proven innocent. Narrowings under a millimetre and a half with climbing bilirubin are dilated with a balloon and brushed for malignant cells. Because new dominants keep appearing, this look inside is repeated every year without fail.
steps.tx: **Dominant stricture** (the tightest PSC segment) under **1.5** mm with rising bilirubin needs **balloon dilation** (endoscopic stretching) with brush cytology because of cancer risk, repeated annually. Incomplete opening earns a temporary stent, and tissue diagnosis precedes any operation, since cancer changes everything.

steps.say: IgG4 disease mimics cancer so closely that surgeons have removed benign strictures thinking them malignant. The clues are sky high serum IgG4 over one thirty five with a diffusely swollen sausage pancreas. A short steroid trial melts both duct and pancreas swelling, which no cancer ever does. Relapses are moved to rituximab maintenance.
steps.tx: **IgG4** sclerosing cholangitis (steroid-responsive fibroinflammatory duct disease) with **IgG4** above **135** mg per dL plus a sausage pancreas, melting with prednisolone **0.6** mg per kg, told apart from cancer by **steroid trial** (shrinkage on steroids proves benign disease). Relapse needs rituximab or azathioprine maintenance.

vis.alt: Diagram and micrograph showing IgG4 biliary stricture, sausage pancreas and storiform fibrosis.
vis.caption: IgG4 disease pairs strictures with sausage pancreas and melts on steroids. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: In Southeast Asia, stones form inside the liver itself and keep infecting the ducts year after year. Pigment stones pack the intrahepatic ducts above tight strictures, rotting the segments they drain. Antibiotics alone are never curative. The dead segments come out with a Roux loop left behind so future stones can be reached endoscopically.
steps.tx: **Recurrent pyogenic cholangitis** (Oriental cholangiohepatitis with intrahepatic stones) with pigment stones and strictures needs hepatectomy for atrophic segments with **hepatolithiasis** (stones inside the liver) plus a biliary access loop. Resection removes the stone factory, and the loop preserves endoscopic access.

steps.say: Worms can live in the bile duct and bring patients back with cholangitis again and again. Roundworms come up from the gut while liver flukes stay in for years. Both are pulled out endoscopically with deworming tablets alongside. Chronic fluke infection is premalignant, so these patients join cancer surveillance.
steps.tx: Worms in the bile duct with **Ascaris** (roundworm wandering up from the gut) or **Clonorchis** (fluke from raw fish) bring back cholangitis again and again, cleared by endoscopic pulling with albendazole tablets, while long-standing **Clonorchis** lifts cancer risk. Stool checks guide family treatment and repeat deworming.

steps.say: Cholangitis declares itself in two classic counts that every student must rattle off. Three features, pain with fever and yellow eyes, make the Charcot triad. Add low blood pressure and confusion and the five make the Reynolds pentad, which means pus under pressure and death without drainage. A pentad is never kept waiting.
steps.tx: **Charcot triad** (pain with fever and yellow eyes: 3 features) flags infection while **Reynolds pentad** (those plus low pressure and confusion: 5 features) means pus under pressure needing **urgent drainage** (emergency bile decompression). Pentad mortality stays high even with prompt **organ dysfunction** (failing kidneys, lungs or circulation) support.

vis.alt: Illustrated biliary tree with obstructing stone, reflux diagram and clinical panels.
vis.caption: An obstructing stone with Charcot features needs drainage before Reynolds develops. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Once cholangitis is graded, the clock starts and the grade sets the speed. Failing organs mean drainage within six hours, no negotiation. Stable but infected patients with high fevers and poor response get the next day slot within twenty four hours. Mild cases settle with antibiotics and are booked electively after the inflammation cools.
steps.tx: Severe cholangitis with **organ dysfunction** (hypotension, altered sensorium or renal failure) goes for ERCP inside **6** hours, moderate cases inside **24** hours, and mild disease electively after antibiotics. Fluids with vasopressors run alongside, and failed ERCP converts to percutaneous drainage.
